svg.title: The NFC ring reality check — what it refuses to do, and what it does forever
svg.desc: Two columns. Left, what a passive NFC ring will never do: no battery, no screen, no heart-rate or step counting, no Bluetooth, and no across-the-room wizardry — it wants to nearly touch the reader. Right, what it quietly does forever: taps doors, terminals and phones at 1-3 centimetres, stores the same NDEF records as any NFC sticker — URLs, vCards, Wi-Fi credentials — is writable when built on NTAG213 or NTAG216, and keeps working 10-plus years without a single charge.
svg.text: Not a wand, not a watch — a very patient tag

g.text: ✗ Bluetooth or an app of its own
it wants to all but touch the reader

svg.text: it will never nag you to stand up —

g.text: ✓ taps doors, POS terminals and phones
at 1–3 cm, in under a second
✓ stores NDEF like any NFC sticker:
✓ harvests power from the reader's field —
10+ years of data retention, zero charging

svg.text: always on the hand — no card, phone
or badge to find and present
Active sensor rings exist — different animal, different guide. This one is about the tag that never needs feeding.
